title: Lena and the Summit
premise: Lior Vasquez, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted after a client's death they insist wasn't their fault, takes a last job escorting a grieving heiress, Lena Okonkwo, to a coastal village where her estranged grandmother's will names her heir to 'the source.' When an extreme low tide exposes a sea cave marked with the grandmother's climbing sigils, Lior and Lena discover the inheritance is a route: a river running beneath a glacier to a forbidden alpine cirque, passable only in the narrow window before calving season. Racing rival claimants and their own mistrust, they reach the source and find the grandmother's final camp — and proof that the death that ruined Lior was caused by the same rival guide who now hunts them. Exposed, the rival's blacklist-worthy record surfaces, and Lior returns not cleared by paperwork but trusted again, choosing to stay as the village's new guide while Lena claims a belonging she never expected.
about_author: Yara Coldharbour is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent six seasons feeding climbers on three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the mountains refused to spit back out.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Broke and unemployable in two countries, Lior accepts a sketchy contract from a lawyer: escort Lena Okonkwo to the fishing village of Salt Hollow for a will reading. The emotional beat is bitter pride wrestling with desperation; Lior tells themselves it's just money, but the mention of the grandmother's name — a legend of the range — hooks something older.

chapters.title: Salt Hollow
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Arriving in the village where her grandmother once lived, Lena meets hostile locals who blame her family for abandoning the community, and a will that grants her only 'the source, if she can find it.' The emotional beat is alienation: she inherits nothing but a riddle and a town's resentment.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A once-in-a-decade spring tide drains the bay, revealing a sea cave carved with climbing sigils matching the grandmother's old journals. Inside: rope, a rusted tin box, and a map following a river upstream into forbidden glacier country. The beat is awe curdling into dread as Lior recognizes the route that killed their last client.

chapters.title: Rivals on the Ice Road
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Word leaks; a rival outfit led by charismatic guide Soren Hale — the man whose testimony blacklisted Lior — files competing claims and buys the village's silence. Lena realizes the 'family' she resents may be her only protection. The beat is first trust: she asks Lior to take her upriver, against every rule.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two set out along the river gorge, racing the calving season window. A storm forces them into a shared bivouac where Lior finally tells the truth about the client's death — and Lena admits she never knew her grandmother at all. The beat is two liars trading honesty like currency.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They reach the cirque: a hidden valley with the grandmother's final camp, letters addressed to Lena across twenty years, and evidence she'd been documenting Soren's falsified safety records — including the one that doomed Lior's client. The beat is grief transformed into purpose; the inheritance was never land, it was testimony.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Soren's team catches up, and the glacier begins to calve early, collapsing the exit route. In the chaos, Soren tries to seize the letters as evidence against himself. The beat is terror and clarity: Lena chooses the letters over the escape line, nearly dying for them.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With the main route gone, Lior must lead an unroped descent of the grandmother's original escape gully — the climb that made her a legend and killed her partner. Lior confronts the fear that has ruled them since the accident. The beat is redemption through competence: guiding done right, at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Back in Salt Hollow, the letters and Soren's forged records go public. The village that scorned her reads its own history in her grandmother's hand, and the association reinstates Lior. The beat is vindication that feels less like victory than homecoming.

chapters.title: The Source Is a Door
chapters.summary: Shared POV. One year later: Lior runs the village guide service, Lena has restored the grandmother's hut at the cirque as a refuge station, and the tide cave is mapped and protected. On the anniversary low tide, they walk into the cave together — no longer heirs or outcasts, but keepers. The beat is belonging, chosen and earned.
